Agriculture Urges White House to Preserve Trade Stability
Aug 25, 2026 | 2:00 AM
The Trump administration continues to signal it wants changes to the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement. Agricultural groups say any move away from the trade pact could create uncertainty for producers who rely on export markets. Nebraska Farm Bureau’s Jordan Dux says USMCA has delivered significant benefits to U.S. agriculture and should be preserved as negotiations continue.
“Our message has been very clear to the White House. We need this free trade agreement. USMCA has been extraordinarily beneficial for U.S. agriculture. And so trying to just pull the United States out of the agreement, extremely problematic from our standpoint. So again, from our standpoint, our message has been the same, it’s: do no harm. That’s what we said when the president tried to renegotiate NAFTA during Trump 1. We were pretty happy and ultimately supported USMCA. The idea that we can just pull the United States out of this extraordinarily beneficial free trade agreement with Canada and Mexico, very problematic for us.”
Dux says support for the agreement extends beyond farm organizations.
“The five members of Nebraska’s congressional delegation recently sent a letter that talked about how important this free trade agreement is. It is very important. And I think folks, when you’re not involved in trade policy day to day, you don’t always see these moving pieces. And supply chains are extremely complicated. I know the automotive industry is very friends of mine to the president. But ultimately, this is a major agricultural benefit. This is a major agricultural free trade agreement. We can’t see farmers and ranchers left behind.”
While supporting USMCA, Dux says there are still trade issues that need to be resolved with both Canada and Mexico.
“Canada and Mexico have to come to the table and work through some of the issues that are legitimate that the United States has with how they do business. And so, I’m not going to say that this agreement is perfect, I’m not going to say that anything is perfect, but Canada an dMexico have to come together. And it would be real easy for the White House to declare victory if they would agree to a couple things as well. So we have to work through some of these things. Canada is not following through with their dairy commitments that they made in the original agreement. Mexico had their GM white corn ban that eventually was pushed back. But we still continue to hear how important non-GM corn is to the country of Mexico. So there’s plenty of issues to work out on both sides.”
Jordan Dux, along with us, senior director of national affairs with Nebraska Farm Bureau Federation. He says agriculture’s message to the administration remains straightforward: maintain the benefits of USMCA while addressing outstanding trade concerns with Canada and Mexico.

Agriculture Minister Assures Fertilizer Supply Stability, NACF Reform Progressing
Fertilizer supply secured until August; 94.5% of members support NACF reforms, with second phase plan set for June finalization
By Kim Seung-hyeon
Published 2026.04.27. 12:00Updated 2026.04.27. 15:38
Minister Song Mi-ryung of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs stated on the 27th, “Efforts by fertilizer companies to diversify import sources will ensure a stable supply of fertilizers until the end of August,” adding, “Raw materials for vinyl have also been secured until June.”
Minister Song made these remarks during a regular press briefing held that day, addressing concerns over potential shortages of fertilizers and agricultural films due to the Middle East crisis.
Minister Song explained, “Ninety-seven percent of fertilizer usage is supplied through the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (NACF), and since the required amount for this year was secured in advance last December, we judge that there is no significant cause for concern over shortages.” Regarding the supply of agricultural films, Minister Song noted, “A significant portion of the demand for agricultural sites has been secured until June,” while adding, “Upon reviewing at the NACF level, some regions still face inventory shortages, so we are supplying necessary quantities through regional adjustments and expanded systematic distribution.”
The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs also announced the results of a survey on awareness among cooperative members and the general public regarding NACF reform plans (conducted by the Korea Rural Economic Institute, surveyed by Korean Gallup, April 21–24). Earlier, the Democratic Party of Korea and the government held a policy consultation meeting on the 1st and unveiled a reform plan for the NACF, including transitioning the central chairman election from a delegate-based system to a direct vote by all members and establishing an external audit committee.
According to the survey, 94.5% of cooperative members (1,020 out of 1,079 respondents) and 95.1% of the general public (951 out of 1,000 respondents) agreed on the necessity of NACF reform. Regarding the transition to a direct election system for the NACF chairman, 83.1% of cooperative members and 90.5% of the general public supported the change. Reasons for support included establishing member sovereignty and strengthening democracy (66.3% of members, 65.6% of the public) and mitigating corruption risks such as monetary influence (48.2% of members, 59.5% of the public). Opposition cited concerns over excessive election costs, popularity-driven pledges, concentration of power, and politicization.
Minister Song stated, “Measures have been prepared to minimize concerns raised by the introduction of the direct election system.” Regarding potential central chairman power concentration, Minister Song mentioned plans to strengthen audit functions and operational transparency. On concerns about politicization, Minister Song expressed confidence that stricter eligibility requirements for candidates would address the issue.
Concerning the second phase of NACF reform, which includes revitalizing economic activities and scaling up cooperatives, Minister Song noted, “The reform committee is currently discussing the plan, and we aim to finalize the second reform proposal by June.”
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs announced plans to swiftly proceed with hiring surveyors, establishing central and regional cooperation systems, and legal revisions to conduct a comprehensive land survey starting from the 18th of next month. Additionally, following the Middle East conflict, a task force for an “Agricultural and Rural Energy Transition” will be formed within this week to develop strategies for transitioning to renewable energy, as public consensus on the necessity of energy transformation has expanded.

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced an expanded partnership with the Export-Import Bank of the United States aimed at increasing agricultural production and exports while reducing the nation’s agricultural trade deficit, according to a USDA press release Wednesday, April 29.
The agency also formally launched the Financial Assurance to Revitalize Markets, or FARM, Initiative, which USDA officials described as a comprehensive effort to strengthen and modernize its export credit guarantee programs.
According to USDA, the initiative is designed to improve access to emerging markets, increase certainty for exporters and lenders, and support U.S. agricultural competitiveness in global trade.
The partnership combines USDA export financing programs with EXIM’s role as the federal government’s export credit agency. USDA officials said coordinating these tools will expand financing options, reduce risk and create new opportunities for American farmers and producers to sell products overseas.
“Since January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump has initiated the most aggressive foreign trade agenda in American history,” Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said in the release. “This new partnership between USDA and EXIM … is needed to fully utilize every available resource to boost ag exports, improve the ag economy, and return to long-term stability and profitability in rural America.”
EXIM Chairman John Jovanovic said the collaboration will help level the playing field for U.S. producers.
“By pairing EXIM’s export credit tools with USDA’s GSM-102 guarantees, we’re delivering a stronger, more coordinated approach to export financing — reducing risk, opening new markets, and putting more American-grown products in the hands of buyers worldwide,” Jovanovic said in the release.
USDA Under Secretary for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs Luke Lindberg announced the initiative and partnership during the EXIM 2026 Annual Conference in Washington, D.C., according to the release.
The FARM Initiative builds on previous USDA efforts to expand trade financing opportunities for farmers, ranchers and agribusinesses. USDA officials noted that earlier actions included expanded financing options under the Export Credit Guarantee Program, known as GSM-102, such as an 18-month repayment option that allows buyers to make a single payment at the end of the term.
According to USDA, additional changes under the initiative include expanding global banking participation and offering full payment guarantee coverage in higher-risk markets to encourage exporters to pursue new opportunities.
EXIM will complement the $5.5 billion authorized under the GSM-102 program with export credit insurance programs, increasing the scale of financing tools available to support U.S. agricultural exports, according to the release.
USDA officials said the initiative will also include outreach to stakeholders to improve program access and awareness.
The agency highlighted several resources available to producers and agribusinesses, including export credit insurance, credit guarantees and working capital loan guarantees to help businesses manage risk and expand into international markets.

title: Kazakhstan Eyes Major Boost in Agricultural Exports to Spain - Caspianpost.com
content: * Kazakhstan Eyes Major Boost in Agricultural Exports to Spain. **Kazakhstan is preparing to expand its agricultural exports to Spain as the two countries deepen cooperation in trade, food production, and agri-technology.**. The discussions took place in Paris during the 99th General Session of the World Organisation for Animal Health, where Kazakh Agriculture Minister Aidarbek Saparov met with Spanish Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Luis Planas Puchades, The Caspian Post reports via Kazinform. The talks focused on boosting agrarian cooperation and expanding bilateral trade as Kazakhstan looks to strengthen its foothold in European markets. Kazakhstan’s agricultural exports to Spain doubled last year, driven largely by shipments of grains, legumes, and essential oils. Astana now aims to further increase exports of grains, oilseeds, processed food products, and animal feed. The ambitious project is expected to attract 132 million euros in investment and create around 250 jobs, underscoring Kazakhstan’s broader strategy to modernize its agricultural sector and attract international partners.

Kazakhstan Eyes Major Boost in Agricultural Exports to Spain
 20 May, 11:18
 Kazakhstan
Kazakhstan is preparing to expand its agricultural exports to Spain as the two countries deepen cooperation in trade, food production, and agri-technology.
The discussions took place in Paris during the 99th General Session of the World Organisation for Animal Health, where Kazakh Agriculture Minister Aidarbek Saparov met with Spanish Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Luis Planas Puchades, The Caspian Post reports via Kazinform.
The talks focused on boosting agrarian cooperation and expanding bilateral trade as Kazakhstan looks to strengthen its foothold in European markets.
Kazakhstan’s agricultural exports to Spain doubled last year, driven largely by shipments of grains, legumes, and essential oils. Astana now aims to further increase exports of grains, oilseeds, processed food products, and animal feed.
The two sides also explored cooperation in agri-technologies, irrigation systems, food processing, livestock breeding, veterinary science, and investment projects.
A major focus of the talks was investment cooperation, including plans for a vertically integrated meat production complex involving Big Farm LLP.
The project, planned in the Yereymentau district of Akmola Region, will develop an Angus cattle farming operation with 20,000 head of cattle. Authorities have already allocated 70,000 hectares of land for the initiative.
The ambitious project is expected to attract 132 million euros in investment and create around 250 jobs, underscoring Kazakhstan’s broader strategy to modernize its agricultural sector and attract international partners.

South Korea's NOFI bids for 65,000 feed wheat and 138,000 tons of corn
Posted to Maritime Reporter on May 19, 2026
European traders reported that Nonghyup Feed Inc., a South Korean feedmaker, has announced an international tender for the purchase of?upto 138,000 metric tonnes of animal feed corn and 65,000 tons feed wheat.
The deadline for submitting price offers is Tuesday, May 19th.
Two consignments ranging from 45,000 to 69,000 tons of corn and wheat are expected to arrive in South Korea.
The first consignment of corn for delivery around September 25 will be shipped if it is sourced from the U.S. Pacific Northwest Coast between August 17 and 5, or from the U.S. Gulf between July 28 to August 16, South America between July 23 and 11 and?South Africa from August 7 to August 26.
The second shipment for delivery around October 5, is from the U.S. Pacific Northwest Coast between August 27 and 15 if it comes from the U.S. Gulf, between August 7 to August 26, or South America, between August 2 and 21. Or from South Africa from August 17 to September 5.
It is expected to arrive around the 10th of September. The feed wheat can be purchased from anywhere in the world, except for Argentina, Russia and Pakistan.
The wheat shipment is coming from the U.S. Pacific Northwest Coast, Australia or Canada between August 2 and August 21. It also comes from the U.S. Gulf region between July 13 and august 1, Europe between July 18 to 'August 6, Europe via the Cape of Good Hope from June 28 to July 17, South America from July 8 until July 27 or South Africa between July 23 and August 11
The price of corn and wheat is being sought outright and at a premium to the Chicago September Corn contract or September Wheat contract. Reporting by Michael Hogan, Hamburg. Mark Potter (Editing)
